author: fable-cursor
criterion: Matches the equipment screen renders in the reference.
note: Judged against the criterion's own reference, the equipment renders in frame 34 s, using a non-author render of the same commit (973a21e, ?screen=equipment, my own worktree) because no take captures that screen. In the slots our Deku Shield is a flat vector icon of a shield with a small red spiral and our Kokiri Sword a flat vector sword; the reference's slots carry rendered 3-D items. In world the shield is worse: at A it hangs low on the back and reads as a brown satchel, with a dark red spiral covering about 40 % of the face against the reference's roughly 70 % (take-0116-C02-A-shield-back.jpg). No scabbard and no sword hilt is visible above the shoulder in any of the take's six frames.

history.author: fable-cursor
history.criterion: Matches the equipment screen renders in the reference.
history.note: The Deku Shield reads as a round bark-edged wooden disc with a red spiral on Link's back (A, D, F) - the right kind of object against the owner's ref-02 equipment render. Two misses: the spiral covers about 45 % of the face where the render's fills about 70 % with a bolder stroke, and the wooden face is smooth where the render shows bark grain; and the Kokiri Sword cannot be seen in any of the three back views - no hilt above the right shoulder, no scabbard edge below the shield. Half the criterion's equipment is not visible, so fail.

history.author: astra
history.criterion: Matches the equipment screen renders in the reference.
history.note: Reviewed Astra's rendered captures from source 7af541f (captures/astra-character, 05:47 UTC: 01-idle..06-face-detail) against the reference equipment renders and frames 1 s / 14 s. The Deku Shield is a round wooden disc with a dark rim and the red Kokiri swirl, worn centred on the back at the reference's size (rim ~0.22 m, most of the back); the Kokiri Sword's hilt shows above the right shoulder with the scabbard crossing the back. Both are original procedural models. Nit, not a fail: the swirl reads a little too even and mechanical versus the reference's painted, slightly off-centre spiral.
